reason: I'm not handing my real money to an AI pet when nobody's said who pays if it makes a bad call, and on top of that it's a monthly subscription with no price yet. My robo-adviser is cheap, boring and works, so a waitlist for an unpriced paid plan isn't worth my email.
objection: Who is liable if the agent loses money? A downloadable record of its decisions is nice, but it doesn't put my money back. Plus I hate subscriptions, and this one has no price on it.
would_change_my_mind: A named licensed broker holding my money with SIPC coverage, clear written terms on who covers losses the agent causes, and a flat price under about $5 a month that comes out cheaper than what my robo-adviser charges.
